description: Pywaterflood is a Python and Rust package for estimating connectivity between injection and production wells with capacitance-resistance models. Its developer repository documents alternatives with a time constant for each injector-producer pair or each producer. Users fit injection and production histories, predict production and inspect residuals. These calculations can support oil-field waterflood design and operation; the documentation also identifies carbon-dioxide flooding and geothermal applications. Geography, time interval and represented wells are determined by the supplied field records. The source and examples are public on GitHub under BSD-2-Clause, with packages available through PyPI and conda-forge. A limitation is that choosing more pair-specific parameters requires sufficient observations, and a fitted connectivity model is not a detailed spatial reservoir simulator. No directly related catalogue record was established. This review checked repository metadata and the documented fitting workflow without obtaining well histories or assessing prediction accuracy. The code is available free of charge under its stated licence.
